purpose: Canonical machine-readable registry for reusable website UI patterns and AI-agent component selection.

statuses.stable: Approved default inside its declared scope. Reuse before inventing another treatment.
statuses.domain: Approved inside one product/domain family. Do not copy outside that scope without promoting it.
statuses.candidate: Useful pattern under evaluation. Inspect before reuse and do not treat it as a default.
statuses.legacy: Existing compatibility pattern. Do not add new usages.
statuses.deprecated: Do not use. Migrate existing usages when they are touched.

selection_order: Identify the reader task: read, compare, navigate, verify, answer, trace, or remember.
Choose an existing stable component that matches the task.
If none matches, choose a domain component inside the same scope.
Prefer restructuring content or adjusting shared tokens before creating a new component.
Create a candidate component only when the information structure is genuinely different.
Promote a candidate only after a real route, responsive behavior, accessibility behavior, documentation, and validation exist.
anti_patterns: Route-local table styling when study-table already fits.
Paragraph-heavy text compressed into three or more narrow columns.
Meaningful body or metadata text below the documented readability floor.
Cards used for ordinary linear prose.
Repeated horizontal dividers that fragment one explanation.
New page-specific CSS that duplicates an existing component with different spacing or typography.
Competing shared and route-specific selectors that both own the same component.

components.title: Study table
components.intent: Compare structured facts, fields, objects, rules, or assessment knowledge without shrinking text.
use_when: Rows and columns are the clearest representation.
The reader needs side-by-side comparison or scanning.
The content must remain readable on mobile.
avoid_when: The content is an ordered process.
Each row is mainly a navigation destination.
The content is paragraph-heavy and reads better as one or two columns.
accessibility: Wrap wide tables in a focusable table-scroll region with an aria-label.
Use semantic th elements for real headers.
Do not encode meaning only with background color.
responsive: Keep normal text size.
Use horizontal scrolling instead of compressed columns.
Preserve normal wrapping inside cells.

components.title: Page FAQ
components.intent: Present repeated question-and-answer material as a readable native disclosure list.
use_when: The content is naturally phrased as independent questions.
Answers are short enough to scan without a separate article structure.
avoid_when: The answers form one continuous explanation.
The reader must compare all answers simultaneously.
accessibility: Use native details and summary.
Keep a visible focus state through the site focus contract.
Question text remains visible when collapsed.
responsive: Question text stays at readable size.
Answer padding collapses on small screens without narrowing the copy.

components.title: Research section intro
components.intent: Introduce one substantial section with eyebrow, heading, and supporting copy as one readable unit.
use_when: A Labs or research section needs a strong reading entry point.
Heading and explanation should be perceived as one unit.
avoid_when: The heading is inside a compact card or table.
The section is only a short continuation of the previous paragraph.
accessibility: Preserve semantic heading order.
Do not use the eyebrow as the only section label.
responsive: Desktop may center the intro.
Enterprise Context switches to left alignment on narrow screens.

components.title: Boundary note
components.intent: State an important scope, ownership, or interpretation boundary without turning it into a large card.
use_when: One sentence or short paragraph prevents a likely misunderstanding.
The message is contextual rather than a warning state.
avoid_when: The content is a warning, error, or semantic status.
The content needs multiple independent subsections.
accessibility: Icons are decorative unless they add unique meaning.
The text must stand on its own without color.
responsive: The icon and text collapse without reducing reading width.

components.title: Route list
components.intent: Help the reader choose among peer destinations using one clear linked row per route.
use_when: Every entry is primarily a destination.
Entries have comparable information weight.
avoid_when: Rows are facts rather than links.
The content needs sorting, filtering, or dense numeric comparison.
accessibility: Use one primary link target per row.
Keep directional icons decorative.
responsive: Fields stack in source order.
The full row remains a usable target.

components.title: Source register
components.intent: Show source provenance compactly while keeping provider, title, metadata, and action readable.
use_when: The page needs several source records with provenance.
The sources support the content but should not dominate the page.
avoid_when: There is only one ordinary inline citation.
The reader needs a long annotated bibliography.
accessibility: Source title and action remain text, not icon-only.
Metadata must stay above the readability floor.
responsive: Three columns may reduce to two and then one.
Do not reduce font size to preserve the grid.

components.title: Comparison group
components.intent: Compare a small number of conceptual alternatives without forcing long SAP explanations into narrow columns.
use_when: There are two or three related concepts with short-to-medium explanations.
The reader benefits from side-by-side conceptual contrast.
avoid_when: The content is dense enough to require a table.
Each item contains several long paragraphs.
There are more than three peer concepts.
accessibility: Use real headings inside each comparison block.
Do not encode the difference only through color.
responsive: Blocks wrap to two or one column based on available width.
Body copy remains at normal reading size.

components.title: Determination detail
components.intent: Explain one technical determination as a structured record with a small meta rail and readable detail groups.
use_when: One SAP determination needs inputs, rule, output, evidence, and diagnostics together.
The block is a technical record, not ordinary prose.
avoid_when: The content is a simple list.
Several determinations only need one-line comparison.
accessibility: Keep the record heading semantic.
Labels supplement rather than replace explanatory text.
responsive: Header rails collapse before text becomes narrow.
Detail copy stays at readable size.

components.title: Context links
components.intent: Offer a small group of related deep dives without creating another card or navigation section.
use_when: The page needs a compact set of related internal routes.
The links are secondary to the current explanation.
avoid_when: The routes are the main choice on the page.
Each destination needs a description.
accessibility: Keep descriptive link text.
External-style arrows are decorative.
responsive: The row may become a vertical list on small screens.
Do not shrink link text to keep one line.

components.title: Site share panel
components.intent: Offer page sharing and citation actions in a centered, self-contained utility panel that stays readable even when the page canvas is full width.
use_when: The current page should expose standard share and citation actions.
The route uses the default layout and does not explicitly hide site sharing.
avoid_when: A page is an application surface where sharing has no useful reader task.
The same actions are already provided by a more specific product workflow.
accessibility: Keep visible text labels on actions instead of icon-only controls.
Maintain at least 44px action height and a live status region for feedback.
Preserve native button and link semantics.
responsive: The panel owns its own centered width instead of inheriting route-canvas width.
Two columns collapse to one before the action group becomes cramped.
Action labels remain at metadata reading size or larger.

components.title: Compact sequence
components.intent: Present a short ordered learning sequence with a narrow step rail and full reading-width explanation.
use_when: Order matters and each step needs a short explanation.
avoid_when: The sequence is cross-domain enough to need a semantic process map.
The same information is better represented as a table.
accessibility: Step numbers supplement headings.
The reading order follows DOM order.
responsive: Keep the narrow number rail and full-width text column.
